With Detroit's offensive line injuries, quick throws to St. Brown are expected, and Buffalo's defense allowed 111 yards on in-breaking routes in Week 1, an area where St. Brown excels.

Josh Allen is coming off a 334-yard passing performance in Week 1 against the Houston Texans. He now faces a Detroit Lions secondary that is significantly depleted, missing starting safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph, with cornerback D.J. Reed also questionable. The Lions' defense allowed a staggering 410 passing yards in their Week 1 game, indicating a clear vulnerability that Allen and the Bills' potent receiving corps, including DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid, are well-equipped to exploit.

Jahmyr Gibbs played 74% of the Lions' snaps in Week 1 and caught all five of his targets for 30 receiving yards, demonstrating his involvement in the passing game. With Detroit's offensive line facing significant injuries to two starting linemen, Jared Goff is likely to experience more pressure, leading to an increased reliance on check-downs to Gibbs. Furthermore, Buffalo's defensive scheme often concedes underneath yardage to running backs, and the expected game script of the Lions trailing will necessitate more passing, making Gibbs a prime beneficiary.
